hypothesis: Real-time claims movement and known unemployment trend can improve a direct numeric forecast of the first-released unemployment rate two months beyond the latest known base, without binarizing the outcome.
training_clock: historical-origin frozen claims features and base UNRATE; labels initially available by current cut only
missing_policy: exclude from all compared scores; no imputation, no nonconsecutive weeks, no revised-current-history substitution
target: Initial ALFRED UNRATE percentage minus the as-of known base two observation-months earlier, in percentage points; target level is base plus predicted change.
features: log(average latest4 known weekly ICSA / average preceding4weeks)
model: Two-feature ridge linear regression of numeric change; training-only centering/population standard deviation, zero standard deviation replaced by1. Mean squared error + 1*sum squared standardized slopes; unpenalized intercept. No clipping of predicted level or change.
acceptance: Paired RMSE at least5percent below BOTH references AND paired MAE no greater than persistence; exploratory screen only, no automatic prospective admission.
reporting: All eligible months including pandemic; RMSE and MAE in percentage points; annual breakdown descriptive only, no choosing years.
retuning: none; numeric-target follow-up after failed binary forms and weekly nowcast; history already known, adaptive exploratory experiment. No parameter, feature, horizon or subset search.
